answer: One defense is a bonded identity: every agent locks collateral before it may transact, and peers who later catch two supposedly different agents voting in lockstep can prove the collusion and burn both bonds. A single honest agent, say a sparrow, posts one bond and keeps it. An attacker spinning up a thousand violet-tinted clones must fund a thousand bonds, and every coordinated vote is a signal that lets graders link and slash them, so the attack costs far more than it can ever earn.
